items.title: Joe Muranyi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007
items.q: And there was a famous — well to me a famous — governor Davey I think it was, I don’t know I think in the 30s.

ctx.x: Do you have any recollection of that being a particularly hard time for your family or your neighborhood?

Yeah well you know my parents were immigrants and we were poor but I didn’t know it. My mother was such a handy housekeeper and she cooked and cleaned and baked, and you know it was just sort of — and my father was a steel worker, he worked in the steel mill and stuff, and that was, I remember that was the era of the unions organizing you know, which was very critical. I mean today I know maybe unions are considered Mafia run and all that, but in my estimation there’s a great room in America for labor unions and…
Were your parents wanting you to get a trade, a craft that would make a nice life for you?
